It sounded like the start of a 3.0 earthquake. And that was it. And then a second later, there was another loud explosion, and it felt like a 5.(0) earthquake and I thought we were actually having the start of an earthquake."It’s Chevron's second biggest refinery in the U.S.; it supplies a fifth of all motor vehicle fuels and 40% of the jet fuel consumed in southern California.Analysts said it’s unlikely to impact wider oil prices, but due to isolation from other refining centers, the state’s gasoline prices could rise.In addition to Chevron, state and federal safety agencies will investigate the fire after the blaze is extinguished.
